summary: Elevated first-token latency on chat completions after compiler + runtime swap
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLoop reported significantly elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests starting ~2026-03-11 22:10 UTC after their account was routed to the new runtime (runtime-1.9.0) and an upstream compiler swap (jit-compiler v3.4). Impact: ~10-25x increase in median TTFB for short chat prompts, customer-facing timeouts on interactive product flows and increased error rates in client telemetry.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: end-user chat flows in BrightLoop web app (session flow) saw interactive timeouts (client 10s) in ~12% of sessions for a subset of routes.
- Business: brightloop has dedicated capacity; this affects a paid account on reserved capacity (throughput SLA).

Timeline / Observed events:
- 2026-03-11 21:50 UTC: internal rollout of runtime-1.9.0 + compiler swap began for a subset of dedicated pools.
- 2026-03-11 22:06 UTC: BrightLoop's requests first show sharp TTFB increase in our tracing (span: first-token-delivery).
- 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC: BrightLoop opened support channel (#support-brightloop) and reported degraded UX.
- 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC: Support created this ticket and escalated to SRE.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightLoop (dedicated GPU pool: pool-ded-07-usw)
- Platform: runtime-1.9.0 with jit-compiler v3.4, scheduler v2.6, quant profile default-q4_0
- Regions affected: us-west (pool-ded-07-usw)

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer and SRE):
1) Client opens chat session and sends a short prompt (~12 tokens of user text).
2) Redwood API accepts request and routes to model instance in pool-ded-07-usw.
3) Request is accepted but first token is delayed: TTFB recorded between 800ms and 5.2s (median from historical ~90ms to current ~1.8s for same prompt).
4) Longer prompts (>200 tokens) show normal per-token throughput after initial delay.

Logs / telemetry snippets:
- Trace sample (span timings): api-gateway 12ms -> router 8ms -> container-sched 120ms -> runtime-init 1.3s -> first-token 1.45s.
- Exported metrics: first_token_latency.p50 increased from 95ms to 1850ms for pool-ded-07-usw between 2026-03-11 21:30 and 22:10 UTC.
- No OOMs or GPU errors in syslogs. No 5xx surge; 200 responses with delayed first tokens.

Initial hypothesis from SRE/serving team:
- The compiler swap introduced a coldpath where KV cache priming or attention-kernel selection adds synchronous work during initial decode for short inputs.
- Scheduler changes in v2.6 interact with runtime initialization, adding an extra synchronous slo that delays first-token emission for requests that miss the hot-cache.

Investigation notes:
- We reproduced elevated TTFB in staging by deploying runtime-1.9.0 + jit-compiler v3.4 to a dedicated test pool and replaying BrightLoop's traffic (same prompt set).
- When we revert to compiler v3.3 with runtime-1.9.0, TTFB drops back to expected medians (~80-120ms), indicating compiler-change is a strong signal.
- Per-container CPU profiles show a synchronous compile step on first request for a given model shard which is bounded but takes ~700-1200ms. This appears to be triggered even with existing compiled artifacts in some cases (path mismatch in artifact registry).
- Router logs show an increased percentage of requests routed to warm-but-not-primed containers (narrow windows where priming was ongoing).

Workaround / Mitigation applied:
- 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC: Rolled back compiler to v3.3 for pool-ded-07-usw as an immediate mitigation for BrightLoop. Metrics returned to baseline within ~30 minutes.
- Recommended customer-side: increase client first-token timeout to 15s while we complete rollout fixes (temporary).

Next steps / action items:
- (SRE) Add a pre-warm/priming job in rollout pipeline that ensures artifact registry path alignment and triggers priming compile tasks before traffic shift. Owner: Evan Liu, ETA: 2026-03-15.
- (Runtime) Fix artifact path handling in jit-compiler v3.4 to avoid redundant synchronous compile on warm containers. Owner: Marcos Rivera, PR created.
- (Scheduler) Investigate scheduling decision that surfaces containers still in priming state; add routing safety check. Owner: Priya Nair.
- (Support) Notify BrightLoop of rollback and next update window; track UX regressions. Owner: Aisha Patel.

Customer impact / follow-up:
- BrightLoop acknowledged rollback resolved immediate UX issues and requested a postmortem and preventive checklist prior to further runtime/compiler upgrades on dedicated pools.

Resolution (current):
- Temporary rollback to compiler v3.3 applied for affected pool; monitoring confirms TTFB returned to baseline. Full fix pending compiler patch and rollout priming job.
